nodes.label: 63 Steppe (Chile)
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.community_name: Tier C Lossy Folds into Brazil C10
nodes.rationale: No steppe class in Brazil. Folded into 12 Grassland; level-1 parent (10) preserved. Code 63 is reserved in Tier B for Chile's Steppe.

nodes.label: 70 Fog oasis (loma)
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.community_name: Tier C Lossy Folds into Brazil C10
nodes.rationale: No fog oasis (loma) class in Brazil. Folded into 12 Grassland; level-1 parent (10) preserved.

nodes.label: 72 Other crops
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.community_name: Tier C Lossy Folds into Brazil C10
nodes.rationale: 'Other crops' in Bolivia and Peru is not resolved to a crop cycle. Folded into 41 Other Temporary Crops, the Brazilian catch-all; level-1 parent (14) preserved.

nodes.label: 73 Peatland
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.community_name: Tier C Lossy Folds into Brazil C10
nodes.rationale: No peatland class in Brazil. Folded into 11 Wetland; level-1 parent (10) preserved.

nodes.label: 74 Banana
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.community_name: Tier C Lossy Folds into Brazil C10
nodes.rationale: No banana class in Brazil. Banana is a perennial crop, so it folds into 48 Other Perennial Crops; level-1 parent (14) preserved. The Rmd previously sent it to 41 Other Temporary Crops, the wrong crop cycle.

nodes.label: 79 Forest plantation - pine
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.community_name: Tier C Lossy Folds into Brazil C10
nodes.rationale: Brazil does not split forest plantation by species. Folded into 9 Forest Plantation, its own parent class - detail lost but no class boundary crossed.

nodes.label: 80 Forest plantation - eucalyptus

nodes.label: Three-tier harmonisation strategy
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.community_name: Tier C Lossy Folds into Brazil C10
nodes.rationale: How much comparability you get depends on how much detail you give up; rather than one crosswalk the catalog documents three, and every code in every raster has an entry in all three.

nodes.label: Mid-series collection change (Bolivia, Chile)
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.community_name: Tier C Lossy Folds into Brazil C10

nodes.source_location: Which MapBiomas collection is each country?

nodes.label: Rule: no code falls through to 27 Not observed
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.community_name: Tier C Lossy Folds into Brazil C10
nodes.norm_label: rule: no code falls through to 27 not observed
nodes.rationale: 27 means 'MapBiomas could not observe this pixel' and nothing else; the Rmd silently dropped 30 codes into 27.

nodes.label: Rule: no fold may change a pixel's Tier A class
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.community_name: Tier C Lossy Folds into Brazil C10
nodes.norm_label: rule: no fold may change a pixel's tier a class
nodes.rationale: Forces shrubland to 12 Grassland rather than 4 Savanna Formation (4 sits under level-1 Forest, so the other choice would reclassify shrubland as forest and inflate forest area across five countries) and glacier to 33 rather than 25.

nodes.label: Tier B - pan-MapBiomas legend (~50 classes)
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.community_name: Tier C Lossy Folds into Brazil C10
nodes.rationale: Most non-Brazilian codes (13, 29, 61, 66, 68, 81, 82, 34) already mean the same thing everywhere they are published, so Tier B keeps them and only resolves genuine collisions. Right target for continental work needing real thematic resolution; cost is that no single country emits the full legend.

nodes.community_name: Tier C Lossy Folds into Brazil C10
nodes.rationale: Target used by the Trazo Fields extraction pipeline; corrected version of the Rmd crosswalk built under two rules (no fallthrough to 27; no fold changes Tier A class). Lossy by construction for the Andes and Patagonia.

nodes.rationale: Peru files 32 under Non-vegetated while Brazil/Colombia/Venezuela file it under Non-forest natural formation; Tier A follows each country's own legend rather than forcing one. Uruguay's 3 includes closed shrubland. Code 4 means six different things but all under level-1 Forest.

nodes.label: LEVEL1 (six MapBiomas level-1 classes: 1,10,14,22,26,27)
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Read off the hierarchy in each national legend PDF; the shared parents that make Tier A exact.

nodes.label: Code 4: Savanna Formation (Brazil) vs Open forests (Argentina)
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.norm_label: code 4: savanna formation (brazil) vs open forests (argentina)
nodes.source_location: The One Thing That Breaks Analyses

nodes.label: Brazil C10 25 Other non Vegetated Areas
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.norm_label: brazil c10 25 other non vegetated areas

nodes.label: Brazil C10 33 River, Lake and Ocean
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.norm_label: brazil c10 33 river, lake and ocean
nodes.rationale: Chosen over 25 for glacier because every national legend files glacier under level-1 26 Water body.

nodes.label: 22 Non-vegetated area (aggregate, emitted by Paraguay and Uruguay)
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.norm_label: 22 non-vegetated area (aggregate, emitted by paraguay and uruguay)
nodes.rationale: Paraguay and Uruguay emit the level-1 aggregate code 22 (and Paraguay 26 Water body) directly, so those pixels are exact at every tier.

nodes.label: 61 Salt flat (salar)
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: No salt flat class in Brazil. Folded into 25 Other non Vegetated Areas; level-1 parent (22) preserved.

nodes.label: 68 Other natural non-vegetated area
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: No 'other natural non-vegetated area' class in Brazil. Folded into 25; level-1 parent (22) preserved.

nodes.label: Uruguay 3 Closed forest and closed shrubland
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.norm_label: uruguay 3 closed forest and closed shrubland

nodes.label: MapBiomas Peru
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: How the collection was established: Collection 3: stated in the source filenames; 70 Fog oasis and 72 Other crops confirm it. Years 2019-2024.
nodes.source_location: Which MapBiomas collection is each country?

nodes.label: Tier B 32 Hypersaline tidal flat / coastal salt flat
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.norm_label: tier b 32 hypersaline tidal flat / coastal salt flat

nodes.label: Caveat: Peru 32 under 22 vs Brazil/Colombia/Venezuela 32 under 10
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.norm_label: caveat: peru 32 under 22 vs brazil/colombia/venezuela 32 under 10
nodes.rationale: Peru files 32 Coastal salt flat under level-1 22 Non-vegetated area while Brazil, Colombia and Venezuela file 32 Hypersaline tidal flat under level-1 10. Tier A follows each country's own published hierarchy rather than forcing one of the two.

nodes.label: Caveat: Uruguay 3 includes closed shrubland
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Uruguay's code 3 is 'Closed forest and closed shrubland', so Uruguayan level-1 Forest includes shrubland that other countries would place under level-1 10 Non-forest natural formation.

nodes.label: Tier A - MapBiomas level 1 (exact)
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Every national legend is a strict hierarchy under the same six parents; collapsing to level 1 loses detail but never correctness and needs no judgement calls. Use for any statistic that must be defensible across all ten countries.

nodes.label: TIER_B_OVERRIDES (Tier B collision-resolution table)
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: country -> {national code: (tier B code, reason)}; anything not listed is identity. Only genuine collisions are remapped.

nodes.label: Code 63: Shrub and herbaceous mosaic (Argentina) vs Steppe (Chile)
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.norm_label: code 63: shrub and herbaceous mosaic (argentina) vs steppe (chile)
nodes.source_location: The One Thing That Breaks Analyses

nodes.label: MapBiomas Argentina
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: How the collection was established: Collection 2: codes 63, 66, 73 and 77 are Collection 2 legend entries. Years 2019-2024.
nodes.source_location: Which MapBiomas collection is each country?

nodes.label: 66 Shrubland
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: No shrubland class in Brazil. Folded into 12 Grassland rather than 4 Savanna Formation: 4 sits under level-1 1 Forest, so mapping shrubland there would reclassify it as forest and inflate forest area across Chile, Argentina, Peru, Bolivia and Venezuela. In Tier B also absorbs Argentina 63/77 and Venezuela 50.

nodes.label: Argentina 63 Shrubs and herbaceous mosaic
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Tier B → 66, leaving 63 to mean Chile's Steppe unambiguously.

nodes.label: Argentina 66 Closed shrublands
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Kept as 66 in Tier B; Argentina's open counterpart 77 is merged into it.

nodes.label: Argentina 77 Open shrublands
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Tier B → 66, merging Argentina's closed/open shrubland split into the single shrubland class the other legends use.

nodes.label: Venezuela 50 Xerophytic grassland/shrubland
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Tier B → 66 Shrubland so it stops colliding with Brazil's and Colombia's 50 herbaceous sandbank vegetation; Tier C → 12 Grassland (lossy).

nodes.label: Code 4 - six national meanings under level-1 Forest
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.norm_label: code 4 - six national meanings under level-1 forest
nodes.rationale: Savanna Formation (Brazil), Open forest (Argentina, Bolivia, Ecuador), Dry forest (Peru), Wooded savanna (Venezuela), Open Natural Woodlands (Paraguay). All sit under level-1 1 Forest formation so Tier A is unaffected; Tier B keeps the code with the caveat attached.

nodes.label: Code 50 - herbaceous sandbank vs xerophytic shrubland
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.norm_label: code 50 - herbaceous sandbank vs xerophytic shrubland
nodes.rationale: Herbaceous Sandbank Vegetation in Brazil and Colombia but Xerophytic grassland/shrubland in Venezuela: the same code for two unrelated cover types.

nodes.label: Code 63 - Argentina shrub-herbaceous mosaic vs Chile Steppe
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.norm_label: code 63 - argentina shrub-herbaceous mosaic vs chile steppe

nodes.label: Tier B 50 Herbaceous sandbank vegetation
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Kept for Brazil and Colombia; Venezuela's 50 is moved away so the code is unambiguous.

nodes.label: Argentina 63 shrub/herbaceous mosaic -> 66
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Argentina's 63 collides with Chile's 63 Steppe; merged into 66 so 63 is reserved for Chile's Steppe.

nodes.label: Argentina 77 open shrubland -> 66
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Argentina splits shrubland into 66 closed and 77 open; only 66 exists elsewhere, so 77 is merged into it.

nodes.label: Chile stray codes 7 and 16 -> 27
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Not MapBiomas classes: stray pixels in the Chile 2022 raster from non-nearest resampling at mosaic time; treated as Not observed.

nodes.label: Uruguay 19 -> 18 Agriculture
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Uruguay's legend calls agriculture 19 but no raster contains 19; they encode it as 18, so both fold to 18.

nodes.label: Code collision problem (same integer, different meaning)
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.norm_label: code collision problem (same integer, different meaning)
nodes.rationale: The same integer means different things in different countries: 4 has six meanings, 50 is herbaceous sandbank in Brazil/Colombia but xerophytic shrubland in Venezuela, 63 is shrub-herbaceous mosaic in Argentina but Steppe in Chile.

nodes.label: Brazil C10 4 Savanna Formation
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Rejected as target for shrubland because it sits under level-1 1 Forest; accepted only for 67 Dwarf forest, whose level-1 parent is Forest.

nodes.label: MapBiomas Chile
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: How the collection was established: Collection 1: 2019-2022: none of 59, 60, 63, 67 present, and 21 Mosaic of uses is, which the Collection 2 legend does not define; 2022 has mosaic artefacts | Collection 2: 2023-2024: carries 59, 60, 63 and 67. Years 2019-2024.
nodes.source_location: Which MapBiomas collection is each country?

nodes.label: 27 Not observed
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Means only 'MapBiomas could not observe this pixel'; Tier B sends the Chile 7/16 artefacts here because they are not classes.

nodes.label: 59 Primary Forest (Chile)
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Brazil C10 does not separate primary from secondary forest. Folded into 3 Forest Formation; level-1 parent (1) preserved. Tier B label is '?' (no pan-MapBiomas name).

nodes.label: 60 Secondary Forest (Chile)
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: As for 59: Brazil does not separate primary from secondary forest.

nodes.label: 67 Dwarf forest (Chile)
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: No dwarf/krummholz forest class in Brazil. Folded into 4 Savanna Formation, the Brazilian open-canopy woody class; level-1 parent (1 Forest) preserved.

nodes.label: Chile 16 (mosaic artefact, no legend)
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Not in any MapBiomas legend; value sits between 15 and 18. Tier B → 27.

nodes.label: Chile 21 Mosaic of uses
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Present in Chile 2019-2022 but not defined in the Chile Collection 2 legend - evidence those years are Collection 1.
nodes.source_location: Which MapBiomas collection is each country?

nodes.label: Chile 7 (mosaic artefact, no legend)
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Not in any MapBiomas legend; value sits between real codes 6 and 9 - signature of non-nearest resampling upstream. Tier B → 27.

nodes.label: MapBiomas Collection 1 (national)
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.source_location: Which MapBiomas collection is each country?

nodes.label: MapBiomas Collection 2 (national)
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.source_location: Which MapBiomas collection is each country?

nodes.label: Caveat: Chile 2022 mosaic artefacts (4, 6, 7, 13, 16, 32)
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: These codes occur at 1-3 pixels each in a 1-in-16 sample against hundreds of thousands for real classes; values fall between adjacent real codes, the signature of non-nearest resampling during the upstream mosaic. 7 and 16 exist in no MapBiomas legend. Treat all six as no-data for 2022.

nodes.label: Caveat: Chile rasters carry 4, 6, 13, 21, 32 absent from Chile legends
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.norm_label: caveat: chile rasters carry 4, 6, 13, 21, 32 absent from chile legends
nodes.rationale: Names and colours for these come from the pan-MapBiomas standard palette shared by the other national legends.

nodes.label: LUT application snippet (numpy + rasterio)
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Builds a 256-entry uint8 lookup table from harmonization.csv for one country and one tier column, then indexes the raster band; 0 stays 0 (nodata).

nodes.label: Portolan CLI
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Generated the catalog from STAC metadata and .portolan/metadata.yaml; its shipped COG defaults were used with one deliberate deviation (mode resampling) and three additions.
nodes.source_location: What was done to the data

nodes.label: COG conversion of MapBiomas exports
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Source GeoTIFFs exported per country and year from the MapBiomas platform and converted to COGs with Portolan defaults (DEFLATE predictor 2, 512x512 tiles) plus one deviation and three additions.
nodes.source_location: What was done to the data

nodes.label: Provenance tags (MAPBIOMAS_COUNTRY, _YEAR, _COLLECTION, _LEGEND_SOURCE, SOURCE_FILE, OVERVIEW_RESAMPLING)
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.source_location: What was done to the data

nodes.label: legends.json
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Holds the official legend for each of the ten national initiatives.
nodes.source_location: Provenance — legends, harmonisation tables and build scripts

nodes.label: Provenance collection (legends, harmonisation tables, build scripts)
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.norm_label: provenance collection (legends, harmonisation tables, build scripts)
nodes.source_location: Provenance — legends, harmonisation tables and build scripts

nodes.label: Caveat: Paraguay legend colours class 9 as #ffefc3
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.norm_label: caveat: paraguay legend colours class 9 as #ffefc3
nodes.rationale: The Paraguay Collection 2 legend PDF gives 9 Forest Plantation the same colour as the 14 farming aggregate; every other legend uses #7a5900. Reproduced verbatim rather than corrected.

nodes.label: CLASS_<code> TIFF tags
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: The legend travels with the file; one tag per legend entry.
nodes.source_location: What was done to the data

nodes.label: Official MapBiomas colour table per country
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.norm_label: official mapbiomas colour table per country
nodes.rationale: Files render correctly on open in QGIS and ArcGIS.
nodes.source_location: What was done to the data

nodes.label: Overview resampling = mode (deviation from Portolan nearest)
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.norm_label: overview resampling = mode (deviation from portolan nearest)
nodes.rationale: These are categorical maps, where the modal class is the meaningful downsample.
nodes.source_location: What was done to the data

nodes.label: nodata = 0
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: 0 is background/outside-country in every source raster and is not a class.
nodes.source_location: What was done to the data

nodes.label: Data type uint8 (lossless cast)
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Every observed class code is below 256; the full-resolution maximum was verified on each non-uint8 source before casting.
nodes.source_location: What was done to the data

nodes.label: Pixel values not changed - harmonisation is documentation only
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.norm_label: pixel values not changed - harmonisation is documentation only
nodes.rationale: No reclassification was applied to any raster; the harmonisation is documentation to be applied by the reader at analysis time to the tier they need.
nodes.source_location: What was done to the data

nodes.label: Rmd flaw: 30 codes silently dropped to 27
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.norm_label: rmd flaw: 30 codes silently dropped to 27

nodes.label: Unlisted codes become nodata holes
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Anything not listed for a country stays 0 (nodata), so an unexpected code shows up as a hole rather than as a silently wrong class.

nodes.label: TIER_C_FOLDS (Tier C lossy-fold table, tier_b_code -> (brazil code, lossy, reason))
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.norm_label: tier_c_folds (tier c lossy-fold table, tier_b_code -> (brazil code, lossy, reason))
nodes.rationale: Folds applied to any country, expressed against the Tier B code so a collision resolution is applied once; every fold preserves the level-1 parent.

nodes.label: extract_hansen_mapbiomas_v16.Rmd (original crosswalk)
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Original Trazo Fields crosswalk onto Brazil C10. Flaws: drops 30 class codes into 27 Not Observed without saying so; treats Colombia and Venezuela as Brazil-compatible passthroughs although seven of their codes have no Brazilian meaning; sent 74 Banana to 41 Other Temporary Crops, the wrong crop cycle.

nodes.label: Trazo Fields extraction pipeline
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Consumer of Tier C; runs extract_hansen_mapbiomas_v16.Rmd.

nodes.label: MapBiomas Brazil Collection 10
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Tier C target legend. Introduced 6 Floodable Forest, carries 62 Cotton and 75 Photovoltaic, retired code 13; has no glacier, shrubland, steppe, salt flat, peatland, banana, fog oasis or Andean classes and does not split forest plantation by species or primary/secondary forest.
nodes.source_location: Which MapBiomas collection is each country?

nodes.label: Fold 13 / 63 Steppe / 70 Fog oasis -> 12 Grassland
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: No equivalents in Brazil C10; level-1 parent 10 preserved.

nodes.label: Fold 34 Glacier -> 33 River/Lake/Ocean (not 25)
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Every national legend files glacier under level-1 26 Water body; folding to 25 would move pixels to level-1 22 Non-vegetated.

nodes.label: Fold 59/60 primary/secondary -> 3, 67 dwarf forest -> 4
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Brazil C10 does not separate primary from secondary forest; dwarf/krummholz goes to the Brazilian open-canopy woody class; level-1 Forest preserved.

nodes.label: Fold 61 Salt flat / 68 other natural non-veg -> 25
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.norm_label: fold 61 salt flat / 68 other natural non-veg -> 25
nodes.rationale: No such classes in Brazil; level-1 parent 22 preserved.

nodes.label: Fold 66 Shrubland -> 12 Grassland (not 4 Savanna)
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: 4 Savanna sits under level-1 Forest; mapping shrubland there would inflate forest area across Chile, Argentina, Peru, Bolivia and Venezuela.

nodes.label: Fold 73 Peatland -> 11 Wetland; 72 Other crops -> 41
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: 72 'Other crops' in Bolivia and Peru is not resolved to a crop cycle, so it goes to the Brazilian catch-all 41.

nodes.label: Fold 74 Banana -> 48 Other Perennial Crops
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Banana is a perennial crop; the Rmd sent it to 41 Other Temporary Crops, the wrong crop cycle.

nodes.label: Fold 79/80/83 plantation species -> 9 Forest Plantation
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: Brazil does not split plantation by species; folding to the parent loses detail but crosses no class boundary.

nodes.label: Fold 81/82 Andean grassland -> 12 / 11
nodes.author: Tristan Grupp
nodes.rationale: No Andean class in Brazil; a large share of the Bolivian, Peruvian, Ecuadorian and Colombian highlands - flag in any highland analysis.
